# Lingchu Bot 0.2.0

Telegram platform support added. This release introduces the Telegram Bot API
as a second platform front-end alongside OneBot V11, plus a smoke-test
startup fix, a full-project security audit, and a senior-architect
architecture review with P0 remediation.

## Highlights

### Telegram Platform Support

Lingchu Bot now supports Telegram groups alongside QQ via OneBot V11. Five
group-management command handlers (`bot_state`, `menu`, `moderation`, `mute`,
`recall`) are implemented under `handle/telegram/adapters/default/`, mirroring
the OneBot V11 handler surface through the existing `selected_adapter_handle`
decorator and `command_key` permission model.

Telegram permission seeds live in `platforms/telegram/permissions.py` and are
registered through the same platform registry that OneBot V11 uses, so
authorization decisions remain fail-closed and superuser bypass stays
explicit. Event normalization in `hooks/adapters.py` extends the type-safe
`getattr` + `isinstance` pattern with 128-char field limits on
`conversation_id`, `user_id`, and `message_id`.

Platform overview docs are published at
`apps/docs/src/content/docs/platforms/telegram/overview.mdx` (EN + ZH), with
a matching sidebar entry and a Telegram row in the "Available platforms"
table.

### Smoke-Test Startup Fix

Fixed `NameError: name 'GroupMessageEvent' is not defined` on startup. The
root cause was `from __future__ import annotations` in Telegram handler
modules: NoneBot resolves signature forward refs via `wrapper.__globals__`
(the `common.py` module globals), not `func.__globals__`, and `@wraps` copies
`__wrapped__`/`__name__`/`__annotations__` but NOT `__globals__`. Removed
the future-annotations import from the five Telegram handler files and
documented the lesson in `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and
`.github/note/AGENTS-zh.md` under a new "Adapter Handle Decorators"
sub-section so it never regresses.

### Security Audit

A full-project threat model and security audit were completed ahead of the
0.2.0 release. The audit covered the worktree diff and the `src/` baseline,
plus parallel deep sweeps over `services/mcp_server/`, `services/llm/`,
`permissions/`, `hooks/` + `handle/`, and the `lingchu` CLI.

Result: **0 CRITICAL, 0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 1 LOW (pre-existing, accepted),
1 INFO (accepted)**. No remediation was required for the release. The full
report is at
`.trae/specs/prepare-0.2.0-release/security-audit.md`.

Key security properties verified:

- MCP server authentication restricts JWT algorithms to `RS256`/`ES256`
  (no `alg=none` confusion), enforces issuer + audience + expiry +
  not-before, and rechecks grants immediately before writes (TOCTOU
  defense).
- Message query cursors are HMAC-SHA256 signed with `compare_digest`
  constant-time comparison, principal-bound, and TTL-bounded.
- LLM integration redacts credentials from logs and blocks control-plane
  keys (`api_key`, `headers`, `http_client`, …) from prompt-controlled
  payloads.
- SSRF defenses block private/loopback/link-local networks for image
  fetches via `core/http_security.py::validate_public_http_url`.
- Permission resolution is fail-closed; superuser bypass is explicit,
  never wildcard.

### Architecture Review

A senior-architect review of the project from scratch identified 2 P0
findings (both in docs navigation for the 0.2.0 headline feature), 6 P1
findings (architectural smells deferred to follow-up specs), and 5 P2
findings (minor code smells). Both P0s — the docs sidebar missing a
Telegram entry and the "Available platforms" table omitting Telegram — are
fixed in this release. The full report is at
`.trae/specs/prepare-0.2.0-release/architecture-review.md`.

The review also produced four ADR candidates for follow-up: command
definition ownership (`handle/qq/commands/` → `handle/commands/`), single
source of truth for adapter→module-path mapping, migration compat-type
enforcement strategy, and schema generation ownership.

## Fixes

- Fixed `NameError` on startup when Telegram handlers used
  `from __future__ import annotations` (root cause: `wrapper.__globals__`
  vs `func.__globals__`).
- Fixed `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src'` in installed-package
  environments: the `handle/qq/adapters/telegram/default/__init__.py`
  compatibility shim switched from `from src.plugins...` absolute import to
  package-relative `from nonebot_plugin_lingchu_bot.handle.telegram.adapters.default import import_handle`.
